title: POOL machine learning predicts activity of cancer-associated DNA polymerase kappa variants
summary: Partial Order Optimum Likelihood (POOL), a machine-learning method using THEMATICS electrostatic features, was used with the mu4 metric to predict which of 17 cancer-associated DNA polymerase kappa variants affect activity. Biochemical assays showed eight variants (R48I, H105Y, G147D, G154E, V177L, R298C, E362V, R470C) had lower activity than wild type, and nine were similar to wild type. The authors report that POOL predictions identified decreased-activity variants, whereas SIFT, PolyPhen-2 and FATHMM were less able to predict biochemical activity; the variant set is small and accuracy is not quantified in the abstract.
ai_technology: POOL machine learning on THEMATICS electrostatic features to predict variant effects

evidence.tested: Catalytic activity and stability of 17 pol kappa variants were measured and compared with the predictions.
evidence.unknown: Quantified predictive accuracy and generalization beyond 17 variants; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: POOL machine learning predicted which variants would alter activity.
